fullPassage: In his exploration of how we engage with language, John Stuart Mill noted that there is a distinction between the denotation and connotation of words. The denotation of a word is its basic, dictionary definition —the straightforward umbrella term for any entity. For example, the term “human” denotes a person and can be used to refer to all human beings —Alice, Bill, and countless other individuals. To put it another way, denotation is the broad category of actual referents to which a word can be applied. Connotation, on the other hand, is more complicated as it encompasses all the additional attributes and contexts a word can carry that may not be part of its explicit definition. The term “human,” according to Mill, embodies characteristics such as corporeality, biological life, the ability to reason, and a specific external form, and these are what make the word “human” applicable to all the individuals. In essence, grasping the connotation of a word means having a nuanced understanding of the entity the word refers to. By understanding the connotative meanings of a word, one gains a deeper insight into whether a particular object or individual falls within its denotative scope.

지시의미는 어떤 대상에나 쓰일 수 있는 기본적인 사전적 정의이다.
함축의미는 단어의 명시적 정의에 반드시 포함되는 속성만을 가리킨다.
'human'이라는 단어는 신체성, 생물학적 생명 등의 특성 덕분에 모든 개인에게 적용된다.

questions.passage: In his exploration of how we engage with language, John Stuart Mill noted that there is a distinction between the denotation and connotation of words. The denotation of a word is its basic, dictionary definition —the straightforward umbrella term for any entity. For example, the term “human” denotes a person and can be used to refer to all human beings —Alice, Bill, and countless other individuals. To put it another way, denotation is the broad category of actual referents to which a word can be applied. Connotation, on the other hand, is more complicated as it encompasses all the additional attributes and contexts a word can carry that may not be part of its explicit definition. The term “human,” according to Mill, embodies characteristics such as corporeality, biological life, the ability to reason, and a specific external form, and these are what make the word “human” applicable to all the individuals. In essence, grasping the connotation of a word means having a nuanced understanding of the entity the word refers to. By understanding the connotative meanings of a word, one gains a deeper insight into whether a particular object or individual falls within its denotative scope.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④번은 원문과 불일치 — 함축의미를 이해하면 대상 판단에 더 깊은 통찰을 '얻을 수 있다'고 했음
det.analysis:
① 일치 — 지시의미는 실제 지시 대상들의 broad category
② 일치 — 함축의미는 more complicated
③ 일치 — 함축의미 파악은 대상에 대한 nuanced understanding을 갖는 것
④ 불일치 — 원문은 함축의미를 이해하면 대상이 지시 범위에 속하는지 'deeper insight를 얻는다'고 했는데, 진술은 '알 수 없다'로 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: gains a deeper insight를 '알 수 없다'로 뒤집은 정반대 오답

ch: 지시의미는 실제 지시 대상들의 넓은 범주이다.
함축의미를 파악한다는 것은 단어가 가리키는 대상을 섬세하게 이해하는 것이다.
함축의미를 이해하더라도 어떤 대상이 지시 범위에 속하는지는 알 수 없다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② it → its (뒤의 명사구 basic, dictionary definition을 수식하는 소유격 대명사가 필요)
